To prove maximality, let P(n) denote the product. The factorizations of P(2), P(10), and P(12) have greatest common divisor 15: P(2)=3^3·5·7·11, P(10)=3·5·11·13·17·19, and P(12)=3^2·5·7·13·17·19. Any universal divisor must divide this gcd. The proposed modular lower bound and gcd upper bound are valid.

The identities (x+1)(x^2−x+1)=x^3+1 and (x−1)(x^2+x+1)=x^3−1 show that each inner numerator equals its denominator. Each inner fraction is therefore 1 wherever defined, and squaring and multiplying still gives 1. This directly matches cube identities followed by reduction of algebraic fractions.
